label: Figure 8.11: A quota to maintain a minimum price for milk
alt: Milk market with a minimum price above equilibrium and a vertical quota line at Q1, the quantity demanded at that price.
caption: Instead of buying the surplus, the government limits output with a quota set at Q<sub>1</sub> = 30 million litres, the quantity consumers demand at P<sub>min</sub> = $18. Farmers would like to supply Q<sub>2</sub> = 80 at that price, but only Q<sub>1</sub> may legally be sold, so the price holds at P<sub>min</sub> with no surplus. Only the farms allowed to sell within the quota gain.
